items.title: Abbott to spin off its global Nutrition business as an independent listed company
items.summary: Abbott plans a tax-free spin-off of Nutrition (Ensure, Glucerna, PediaSure, Pedialyte, Similac): about $8.5bn sales, 16,000 staff, 14 plants. CEO-designate Daniel Salvadori. Abbott keeps devices, Libre, diagnostics and established medicines (about $42bn).

items.title: Chickenpox vaccination catch-up campaign launched for children
items.summary: An NHS catch-up vaccination campaign offering protection against chickenpox to all children aged four to six years is being launched this week.

items.title: Plans to cut community nurses from children’s service dropped
items.summary: Proposals to cut community staff nurses from Suffolk’s Healthy Child Service have been revised by the county council following a public consultation. Suffolk’s Healthy Child Service currently covers health visiting, school nursing and support for young parents.

items.title: System that spots deteriorating children to be rolled out in England
items.summary: The world’s largest “early warning system” to help staff spot when a child is dangerously deteriorating is being rolled out across England.

items.title: Skincare trends: how nurses can guide children and young people
items.summary: Given the physiological differences in the skin of children and young people compared to adults, elaborate multi-step skincare routines – which have become increasingly popular on social media – can risk damaging the skin barrier rather than protecting it.

items.title: Concerns raised over end of funding increase requirement for children’s mental health
items.summary: A decision to end specific ring-fenced funding increases for children and young people’s mental health services undermines the Government’s commitment to reduce waiting times in this group, a think tank has warned.

items.title: Deprivation worsens mental health in children with intellectual disabilities, study finds
items.summary: Children and young people with intellectual developmental disabilities (IDD) from disadvantaged backgrounds are more likely to experience mental health difficulties, according to new research led by University College London (UCL).

items.title: A guide to common childhood illnesses: chickenpox
items.summary: Chickenpox (varicella) is a highly infectious viral disease that is usually self-limiting in children but can cause serious complications in adults and vulnerable groups.

items.title: Paediatric lung assessments: tips for practice nurses
items.summary: At a recent Nursing in Practice virtual event, consultant nurse and doctoral researcher specialising in respiratory medicine, Aleksandra Gawlik-Lipinski, offered advice and guidance on paediatric lung assessments.

items.summary: The first needle-free adrenaline treatment for young children is now available in the UK. items.title: GPs given new legal duties to proactively share information for child safeguarding
items.summary: GPs are now legally required to proactively share information about children with other safeguarding organisations where there are concerns about their welfare, even if they are not yet at risk of harm.

items.title: Nurses helping orphaned children of colleagues stay in education
items.summary: Hundreds of orphaned daughters of nurses living in developing countries have been able to access education thanks to a charity's nurse mentorship scheme and funding.

items.summary: More than one in four children on waiting lists for community health services in England have been waiting at least a year for treatment, according to new analysis by The King’s Fund. items.title: A guide to common childhood illnesses: threadworm
items.summary: Threadworm (enterobiasis) is the most common parasitic worm infection in the UK, particularly affecting primary school-aged children. Transmission occurs via the faecal–oral route following ingestion of microscopic eggs, which can survive on surfaces for up to 2 weeks.

items.title: Children’s health at ‘crisis point’ from public health nurse shortage
items.summary: School and public health nurses have been “hollowed out” from England's health services, putting children’s health at risk from a lack of preventative healthcare, a new report has found.

items.title: School nurse workforce falls by almost 40% since 2010, analysis reveals
items.summary: The school nursing workforce has dropped by more than 1,100 professionals in England since 2010, according to a new analysis which has prompted fresh concerns around the preventative and early care that children are missing out on.
